request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Determining the Letter Grade Of a Student [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Construct a program that receives a score from the user and determines the grade as follows:\nA for scores ≥ 90\nB for scores ≥ 80\nC for scores ≥ 70\nD for scores ≥ 60\nF for scores < 60\n [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Read the score [[LINE02]] text = input("Enter a score: ") [[LINE03]] score = int(text) [[LINE04]] #Step 2: Determine the grade for the score [[LINE05]] if score >= 90 : [[LINE06]] grade = "A" [[LINE07]] elif score >= 80 : [[LINE08]] grade = "B" [[LINE09]] elif score >= 70 : [[LINE10]] grade = "C" [[LINE11]] elif score >= 60 : [[LINE12]] grade = "D" [[LINE13]] else : [[LINE14]] grade = "F" [[LINE15]] #Step 3: Print the grade [[LINE16]] print("Grade =", grade) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the score, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE03.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int(). [[LINE03.EXPL2]] Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer. [[LINE05.EXPL1]] We have 5 possible letter grades that are A, B, C, D, and F. We could determine the letter grade for the score by performing four tests that check whether the score range matches the grade A, B, C, or D. If all of these tests fail, then we could conclude that the grade is F.

The conditions that we want to use to test the score range are not mutually exclusive (i.e., more than one of the conditions can be true, for example, if the score is 85, all the conditions that test whether the score is greater than or equal to 60, 70, and 80 evaluate to true) therefore, the order that we perform these tests matters and we should test the general conditions only after we have tested the specific conditions first. The most specific condition that we have is the one that tests whether the score is greater than or equal to 90. The second most specific condition that we have is the one that tests whether the score is greater than or equal to 80, and so on. We use if-else if statements instead of sequential if statements because we should stop performing the tests as soon as we find the test that evaluates to true.
Based on what is explained above, we need to first test if the score is greater than or equal to 90. [[LINE05.EXPL2]] To check if the letter grade is A, we need to check whether the score is greater than or equal to 90. [[LINE05.EXPL3]] If the score is greater than or equal to 90, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped. [[LINE06.EXPL1]] This statement assigns A to the grade (only if score is greater than or equal to 90). [[LINE07.EXPL1]] If the first test fails (i.e., when score is less than 90), we need to test if the score is greater than or equal to 80. [[LINE07.EXPL2]] If the first test fails (i.e., when score is less than 90), the body of the previous if statement will not be executed, instead the program jumps to this else if statement, where we test whether the score is greater than or equal to 80.

If score is greater than or equal to 80, then the body of the else if statement is executed. Otherwise, the body of the else if statement is skipped. [[LINE08.EXPL1]] This statement assigns B to the grade only if the first if statement is false (i.e., when score is less than 90) and the else if statement is true (i.e., when score is greater than or equal to 80). [[LINE09.EXPL1]] If all of the above tests fail, we need to test if the score is greater than or equal to 70. [[LINE09.EXPL2]] If all of the above tests fail, the body of the previous else if statement will not be executed, instead the program jumps to this else if statement, where we test whether the score is greater than or equal to 70.

If score is greater than or equal to 70, then the body of this else if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this else if statement is skipped. [[LINE10.EXPL1]] This statement assigns C to the grade only if the previous tests fail, i.e., when the score is greater than or equal to 70 but less than 80. [[LINE11.EXPL1]] If all of the above tests fail, we need to test if the score is greater than or equal to 60. [[LINE11.EXPL2]] If all of the above tests fail, the body of the previous else if statement will not be executed, instead the program jumps to this else if statement, where we test whether the score is greater than or equal to 60.

If score is greater than or equal to 60, then the body of this else if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this else if statement is skipped. [[LINE12.EXPL1]] This statement assigns D to the grade only if the previous tests fail, i.e., when the score is greater than or equal to 60 but less than 70. [[LINE13.EXPL1]] We need to end the above if-else if statements with an else statement that its body is executed when none of the above tests are true, that is when the score is less than 60. [[LINE13.EXPL2]] The body of the else statement gets executed only if the score is less than 60. [[LINE13.EXPL3]] Note than when we end series of if-else if statements with an else statement, we make sure to execute the body of exactly one of those statements. [[LINE14.EXPL1]] This statement assigns F to the grade only if all of the previous tests fail, i.e., when the score is less than 60. [[LINE16.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Grade =" and the value of variable grade.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters). Preserve the original format and Do NOT add, remove, or change any content beyond translation.
